title: Kafsokalyvia skete: Maximus the flying monk who burned his huts
summary: Ralph tells of Kafsokalyvia skete: Maximus the flying monk who burned his huts, about 2005; about the historical monk Maximus at Greece (the ancient oracle sites), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: this is named in in the honor of one of the saints we have here Saint Kaffa so he was known as Maximus the monk. He was not not Otis Maximus and he was known as a flying monk and he burned his huts and he had these miracles and they were sightings of him flying.

plain: A man named Ralph says that in 2005 he visited Kafsokalyvia, a small monks' settlement on Mount Athos, a Greek peninsula of Orthodox monasteries. According to Ralph, a young monk who looked after the place told him it was named for a saint known as Maximus, a "flying monk" who burned his huts, worked miracles, and was seen flying. If true, it would be one more old account of a holy man rising into the air.
